name: Grid
usage: Card grids, grids of entry points on a home page, two- or three-column forms

props.name: columns
props.description:
Fixed number of columns; when omitted, columns are filled automatically by `minColumn` (responsive to the
width).

props.name: minColumn
props.description: Minimum column width when filling automatically: `sm` 160 px, `md` 240 px, `lg` 320 px.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between rows and columns, as a spacing step.

props.name: padding
props.description: Padding on all sides, as a spacing step; no padding when omitted.

members.name: Grid.Item
members.summary:
A cell that spans several columns (`span={2}`) or the whole row (`span="full"`), such as a wide chart in a
dashboard or a full-width field in a two-column form. Other children of Grid take one column each and need no
Grid.Item.

props.name: span
props.description:
Number of columns the item spans, or `full` for the whole row (from the first to the last column). With
automatic columns (`minColumn`), a number larger than the columns that fit adds columns and overflows the
grid; use `full` for items that must take the whole row.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML element to render (`li` inside a Grid rendered as `ul`).

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: Basic usage
examples.description:
Without a number of columns, the grid fills the row automatically by minimum column width (`md`, 240 px, by
default).

examples.name: TwoColumns
examples.title: Two fixed columns
examples.description: Use a fixed number of columns for two-column forms and details.

examples.name: Spanning
examples.title: Spanning columns
examples.description: `Grid.Item` with `span` makes a cell wider: two columns for a wide block, `full` for the whole row.
